speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have been fatigued, experiencing flank pain, and have a fever following antibiotic treatment for acute sinusitis. To determine if your sinus infection has spread to your kidneys, have you noticed any changes in your urination, such as pain, frequency, or cloudy blood in your urine?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your sinus symptoms improved but the fatigue, fever, and flank pain persisted, do you have any known history of kidney stones or a history of urinary tract infections?

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Pyelonephritis (likely complicated by recent antibiotic exposure or a drug-induced component). The history of rash with amoxicillin followed by resolution on cephalexin suggests an allergic reaction was managed, but the persistent flank pain, fever, and fatigue point strongly to a renal infection, possibly pyelonephritis. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, CBC, and Serum Creatinine. REQUEST IMAGES: Renal Ultrasound.
